data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical immunomodulators & antipsoriatics_

**Class:** Distillation product of coal (crude coal tar 1–5%; liquor carbonis detergens 5–20%)

## Mechanism of action
- Aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonist → normalises keratinocyte differentiation (restores filaggrin), antiproliferative, anti-inflammatory, antipruritic; photosensitises to UVA

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic plaque and scalp psoriasis, palmoplantar psoriasis, atopic dermatitis (lichenified), lichen simplex, seborrhoeic dermatitis
- Goeckerman regimen (crude coal tar + UVB, inpatient)
- Tar baths (Ingram regimen)

## Dose & formulations
- Crude coal tar 1–5% in petrolatum or zinc paste; LCD 5–20% in creams, shampoos and bath additives; apply at night

## Adverse effects
- Smell, staining, folliculitis (tar acne), irritant dermatitis, phototoxicity ('tar smarts'), keratoacanthomas/carcinogenicity (occupational, theoretical with therapy)

## Contraindications
- Erythrodermic/pustular psoriasis, infected skin, pregnancy (relative)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (theoretical carcinogenicity).

## Viva points
- AhR ligand; Goeckerman regimen (tar + UVB)
- Tar folliculitis and phototoxicity

_Sources: Khopkar ch.28 (Coal tar); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
